# Generative Adversarial Networks: Architectures, Loss Functions, and Techniques Driving Hyperrealistic Media Synthesis | by Cogni Down Under | Medium. # Generative Adversarial Networks: Architectures, Loss Functions, and Techniques Driving Hyperrealistic Media Synthesis. Image 2: Cogni Down Under. Among deep generative models, generative adversarial networks (GANs) uniquely produce strikingly realistic synthetic samples that often fool even human observers. Under the hood, GANs train two competing neural networks — a generator and discriminator — in a minimax game until outputs are indistinguishable from original data distribution samples. In this article, we’ll do a technical deep dive on modern GAN architectures, specialized training procedures, evaluation metrics and emerging techniques pushing the boundaries of realism in conditional image and video generation. Now let’s examine the GAN components enabling this generative potential. GAN Architectures and Training Losses. 💡Vanilla GANs — Original formulation pits a generator network directly against a binary classifier. ⛓ Conditional GANs — Class labels condition both networks to produce specified output types. 🎯 Wasserstein GAN — Earth mover distance loss provides better gradient behavior. **VQ-GAN**— This variant uses vector quantization to compress the generator’s representations into a discrete latent codebook. **StyleGAN** — In this architecture, the generator has an adaptive style mapping network prior to synthesis. *   Self-supervised GANs — Leverage unlabeled data more efficiently. *   GAN compression — Distill huge models for edge devices. *   GAN steering — Interpolate semantics for control. *   GAN painting — Interactive image editing via latent vectors. *   GAN music — Generate coherent sounds and melodies. *   what techniques enable gan image editing? *   how do vq-gans enable high-resolution generation? *   how to generate and evaluate GAN art for creative industries. *   benchmarking vector quantized GAN performance for efficient generation. In summary, the U-Net architecture, enhanced with timestep embeddings, skip connections, residual blocks, suitable normalization and activation functions, and often self-attention mechanisms, provides a powerful and flexible framework for the core noise (or score) prediction task in diffusion models. * U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation, Olaf Ronneberger, Philipp Fischer, Thomas Brox, 2015 *Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention – MICCAI 2015*, Vol. 9351 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.1505.04597 - Introduces the U-Net architecture with an encoder-decoder structure and skip connections, which became foundational for image-to-image tasks, including noise prediction in diffusion models. * Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alex Nichol, 2021 *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)*, Vol. 34 DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2105.05233 - Details architectural choices for U-Nets in diffusion models, including self-attention layers, Group Normalization, and effective timestep conditioning, leading to significant improvements in image synthesis quality. * High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models, Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Patrick Esser, Björn Ommer, 2022 *CVPR 2022* DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2112.10752 - Introduces Latent Diffusion Models, which adapt the U-Net architecture to a latent space, incorporating self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms for high-resolution, conditional image generation.

results.content: ## Deep Learning Image Generation with GANs and Diffusion Model. Assuming the discriminator is already optimal, when minimizing the GAN objective function, if two distributions are very distant (i.e. if the generated image has distribution far away from the ground truth), the divergence would be large, but the gradient of the divergency would eventually diminish. The shortcoming of Inception Score are: (1) cannot detect mode collapse, e.g. the model can just generate one realistic image for each class, (2) no comparison to real images, (3) poor score to images that are genuinely high entropy, e.g. multiple items exist in the image. A discriminator is used to distinguish the HR images and backpropagate the GAN loss to train the discriminator and the generator. For the Content Loss, a VGG-19 network is used as a feature extractor, and each generated SR (fake) image’s VGG output and its original HR (real) image’s VGG output VGG are compared pixel-wise (and MSE is calculated). The discriminator model takes real images from Domain and generated images from Generator to predict whether they are real or fake. 1. Adversarial Loss: Apply Adversarial Loss to both the Generators, where the Generator tries to generate the images of its domain, while its corresponding discriminator distinguishes between the translated samples and real samples. Fine-tune a trained diffusion model (trained on a dataset from the same or a different domain) on a target dataset, so that it can generate target images. While a conditional model can takes additional inputs to control the generation process, the Guidance technique can control a trained unconditional model, i.e. the generated image at each step in the generation process is pushed to lower loss according to the guidance function (a user-defined loss function). During training, text conditioning is sometimes kept blank, forcing the model to learn to denoise images with no text information (unconditional generation). During training, it is worth mentioning that a pre-trained VAE encoder is used to generate VAE latent tensors as inputs to a U-Net (rather than using full-resolution images) for lower memory usage, fewer layers needed in the U-Net, and faster generation time.
